description: This dataset describes the treatment trains of 609 publicly owned wastewater treatment works in California, unit process by unit process. The configurations were extracted from National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System and Waste Discharge Requirement permit documents dated 2004 to 2025 with an ontology-guided large language model (the Water Treatment ontology and GPT-5 Mini), and supplemented with Clean Watersheds Needs Survey data for 355 plants; 318 plants have both, so permit-based and survey-based inventories can be compared. Each record marks whether a process is present, past, planned or off-site across primary and secondary treatment, nutrient removal, disinfection, filtration and solids processing. It was produced by Stanford's WE3 Lab and published in the Stanford Digital Repository in June 2026 under the MIT licence, with the extraction code on GitHub. Caveats: coverage is one state, processes are machine-extracted from permits and may contain errors, and flows and capacities are not the focus. Simulation uses: plant configurations for treatment process models and digital twins, capacity planning and greenhouse gas inventories. Related records: the Clean Watersheds Needs Survey (data-epa-clean-watersheds-needs-survey-2022) and HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste).
